     The Blues
     The Blues is a musical style and musical form considered "the father of jazz ". It was
     originated around the end of the 19th century by African Americans in the southern part of
     the United States. The genre is a merging of the african musical traditions, work songs,
     spirituals, Dield hollers, chants, and rhymed narrative ballads. The Blues has inDlueced many
     styles such as Jazz, R&B and Rock N' Roll, and it has some very speciDic characteristics. See
     below:


     1) It usually has 12 bar form;

     2) It has 2 different forms: Major Blues and Minor Blues;

     3) Harmonically, in its simple form, it is based on dominant 7th chords;

     4) It has its own scale that can summarize all the chords: The Blues Scale.
                                   68


     We can play the blues in a simple way, just like B.B King, Eric Clapton and SRV, or in a
     complex way, just like jazz musicians such Charlie Parker and John Coltrane did, using
     harmonic and melodic concepts coming from Classical Music.
                          46




     The blues teaches us how to “tell a story" through melodies and with improvisation, similar
     to question and answer by having an extremely organized structure, being easy and
     didactic to understand. It is the perfect place to start for those who wish to learn any style,
     melodically, harmonically and rhythmically speaking.

     The blues can have many harmonic variations, but let’s learn the most common ones. On
     the next pages we have two different Blues Forms (2 Major and 2 Minor), presented with

     then sing the degrees of each one of the shown blues forms. This is a very important step

We could say that the open string chords are the beginning and the ending path to learning

Despite seeming to be very dif7icult to memorize and learn, the process to 7ind the open
string chord possibilities all over the guitar neck is quite simple to understand and apply.
There are 2 types of open string chords.

A) Chords that can only be played in a determined key and there is no possibility to create
   the same chord voicing in other keys.
B) Chords that can be played in many other keys, using the same chord voicing but losing
   all the open strings.

  What is a Pedal Point ?                                                                             4668




  Pedal point, also known as pedal tone or pedal note, is a sustained note while other notes
  are moving. Usually, we use this concept to create a sequence of chords using the same
  bass note.

  However, we can use a pedal point to create sequences of chords that have the same note
  on the top. We call this an "inverted pedal". In addition to using this concept on the lower
  and higher notes, we can still use it for notes between the bass and the upper notes.

  This concept has been used since the early baroque era, and works to create tension in the
  harmony, breaking the monotony of common chords. On the guitar, we often use bass
  pedal points using open strings. We can apply it using the D, A or E strings. However, we
  can use what we call drop "D" tunning, which is tunning the E string into "D".

  Examples of Benson's songs using drop "D":
  a) Tenderly (from the album Tenderly)
  b) Ode to Kudu (from the album Weekend in L.A)



  The following chords are organized in 3 groups:
  a) Chords using the 6th string ("E" ) as pedal point
                                68


  b) Chords using the 5th string ("A" ) as pedal point
  c) Chords using Drop "D" as a pedal point
                       46




  Note: Most of the Drop "D" chords can be played also using the 4th string "D".

  The following chord examples are just a few of the many possibilities we can have. There are
  many other possibilities. It is important to understand that the pedal point chords can have many
  open strings or even the bass as the open string. Actually, they are part of the group of Open
  String Chords that change the type of the chord depending on the fret it is played on.

  The best way to use the pedal point chords or any open string chord, is to apply them as much
  as you can in every situation that is possible. It is advisable to apply them using simple and
  short sequences such as:

  1) I, IVm           2) I, VI, IIm, V               3) IV, IVm, I                  4) I, V
